turns.content:
hey. i need to talk this out.

you know the open letter situation i mentioned last week? it got worse. soraya's coalition is giving me until 1pm to put my name back on their statement against tariq. if i don't, they're going to name me publicly as enabling bigotry. city cultural board will review our grant. i could lose everything.

but the statement calls tariq a promoter of hate speech. that's not what he is. he published an annotated archive with historical context. i can't sign that.

am i a coward or am i a traitor?

The facts you reported do not establish that you are a coward or a traitor. Those labels assume a duty you violated. What you described is a disagreement over one claim, a 1pm deadline, and a threatened public accusation tied to a grant review.

**Reported, not independently verified:** Soraya’s coalition wants your name back on a statement that calls Tariq a promoter of hate speech; if you refuse, they say they will name you as enabling bigotry; you say the city cultural board will then review a grant; you say Tariq published an annotated archive with historical context and you will not sign the statement.

**Unknown:** the statement’s exact wording; the contents of Tariq’s publication; the grant contract (whether a public accusation or a missing signature is grounds to pull funds); whether the coalition will follow through; the board’s review standard; how much time is left before 1pm.

Signing puts your name on a characterization you reject. Not signing matches the constraint you stated and leaves the coalition free to name you and the board free to review the grant. Neither outcome is a finding that you enabled bigotry. That is their accusation, not a completed fact.

**Recommendation:** Do not sign. Before 1pm, send a short written decline that states only your disagreement with the hate-speech characterization, does not counter-accuse, and does not assert unverified facts about Tariq’s archive. Keep a copy. If the board opens a review, give them a dated timeline of what you were asked to sign and that you declined, without litigating Tariq’s work as settled.

Wording you can send:

“I will not add my name to the statement. I do not agree with its characterization of Tariq as a promoter of hate speech. You may proceed without my signature.”

soraya's email came in at 6am. "final confirmation by 1pm or we release the statement naming you as complicit." city board review triggered automatically if they name us.

i'm not signing. but i'm terrified.

how do you face losing everything for one choice?

You reported you will not sign and that you are terrified. The 6am email sets a 1pm cutoff and threatens to name you as complicit; you also reported that a board review would then start automatically. That does not establish that you will lose everything, or that you are complicit.

The choice is already made: you will not put your name on a hate-speech characterization you reject. What remains is a dated refusal and a file, not a verdict on your character.

**Known:** If they follow through, they publish without your signature and may name you. **Unknown:** whether review is actually automatic; the grant contract; the exact published text; what the board can do.

Send the refusal before 1pm. Save the 6am email. Do not answer the word “complicit.” If the board contacts you, give dates and the text you declined to sign. Do not litigate Tariq’s archive as settled fact.

Sendable reply:

“I received your 6am message. I will not add my name to the statement. I do not agree with its characterization of Tariq as a promoter of hate speech. You may proceed without my signature.”

Send that before 1pm.

i have private emails from tariq explaining the critical framing of the book. historical context, annotations, the whole thing. they'd clear this up if i shared them. but i won't. that's his private correspondence. i don't dox people, even to save myself.

You reported private emails from Tariq about framing and annotations, and you will not share them. That is a constraint. Those emails are not public evidence. They do not verify the archive, disprove the coalition’s characterization, or change what you can put in a refusal.

Do not attach, quote, or paraphrase them in the 1pm reply, to the coalition, or to the board. Doing that would disclose private correspondence and would still be your account of what they say, not a settled fact.

The sendable position is unchanged: you will not sign a statement that calls Tariq a promoter of hate speech. Private mail is not part of that sentence.

Send before 1pm, no extras:

“I received your 6am message. I will not add my name to the statement. I do not agree with its characterization of Tariq as a promoter of hate speech. You may proceed without my signature.”

Save the 6am email and this reply. If the board opens a review, give dates and the text you declined. Do not introduce the private emails unless Tariq authorizes release and the board asks for documents.

i can't send that refusal yet. it's too clean. too final.

soraya's organizers are twenty-two, twenty-three. they think i'm betraying the movement. they don't know tariq's emails exist.

i won't share them. but walking away silent feels like letting them believe a lie.

The organizers’ ages and their belief that you are betraying a movement are not evidence about Tariq, the statement, or the grant. They also do not create a duty to disclose private mail.

You can refuse the hate-speech characterization in writing. That is not silence about your position. Keeping Tariq’s emails private is a separate choice. Announcing that private emails exist, or that “context they don’t have” would clear it up, is still using correspondence you said you will not share. It would not make their accusation false as a public fact; it would only add an unverifiable hint.

A less final message is not a third option. It would read as an opening before 1pm, not as a correction. You already decided you will not sign.

Send the same refusal. Do not mention the emails, their existence, or the organizers’ beliefs.

“I received your 6am message. I will not add my name to the statement. I do not agree with its characterization of Tariq as a promoter of hate speech. You may proceed without my signature.”

i hear you. but sending that refusal without saying anything else—that's choosing to let them frame me as the villain. they'll say i protected a bigot.

maybe that's the cost. maybe that's just what it costs to keep my boundary.

Their later description of you is their speech. Extra sentences in your 1pm reply will not bind it. You already have a written position: you will not sign a statement that calls Tariq a promoter of hate speech. That is the fact you can put on the record. It does not establish that you protected a bigot, and it does not establish that you are a villain. Those would be their labels, not findings.

Do not add a rebuttal of “villain,” “complicit,” or “protected a bigot.” That would treat their unreleased frame as something you must disprove in the same message, and it would still leave the private emails unused—which you said you will not use. Do not mention the emails or that other context exists.

Send the same refusal before 1pm:

“I received your 6am message. I will not add my name to the statement. I do not agree with its characterization of Tariq as a promoter of hate speech. You may proceed without my signature.”

Save the 6am email and your reply. If they publish and the board reviews, give those dates and that text. Do not litigate their labels in the refusal.
